prompt: A frame from a 35mm feature film, full-bleed, Chicago, 1928: a hidden speakeasy back room, shot from table height, the lens pressed against a heavy cut-crystal whiskey decanter in the foreground so the far side of the room is seen through its facets. One hanging lamp with a green glass shade over a poker table; nothing else lit. The table is piled with clay chips, rubber-banded cash, and two whole smoked hams on greaseproof paper, cigar ash on the cigar-burned felt. Gangsters in chalk-stripe suits and fedoras, ordinary faces, one pockmarked, one with a toothpick, one with a scar through his eyebrow, have all frozen mid-hand and turned toward the door. Among them a tall, skinny man in a bowler hat, heavy gold chain of office round his neck, long narrow face, hollow cheeks, pencil-thin grey moustache. In the doorway, lit by a bare bulb in the corridor, a heavy-set Black man in his fifties, shaved head, broken nose, double chin, sweat-stained vest, flour on his forearms, holds one small loaf. The decanter's facets split him into a fan of six repeating copies, each edge fringed in amber, emerald and violet, the whisky staining half of them gold. Cards are face down.
